findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - production unwrap on fallible I/O result
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (permission denied, missing file, disk full) panics the calling thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return a Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - production unwrap on fallible parse result
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input (non-numeric value in field 1) panics the calling thread instead of returning a typed Parse error
findings.fix: Use .parse().map_err(|e| ParseError::...) and propagate via Result return

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast on parsed u32 value
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..=u32::MAX silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect data without any indication of loss
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from() or u32::checked_into::<u16>() to detect out-of-range values and return a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Empty or single-field lines panic with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0) or split_once(',') with match/ok_or

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Lines with only one comma-separated field panic with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1) or split_once(',') with match/ok_or

findings.problem: println!() side effect in data-loading function - hidden I/O in core
findings.failure_mode: Violates functional core / imperative shell boundary; makes the function non-deterministic, untestable without capturing stdout, and couples data loading to console output
findings.fix: Remove println! from core logic; emit log events at the imperative shell boundary if needed

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no error type - all failures are panics
findings.failure_mode: Every possible failure (I/O, parse, out-of-range, malformed line) aborts the program rather than returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: Change signature to fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> with a typed error enum covering I/O, Parse, Range, and MalformedLine

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then as u16 - unnecessary wide parse followed by lossy cast
findings.failure_mode: Parses to u32 unnecessarily (wider than needed), then truncates with as, combining two bugs: wasted computation and silent data loss
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16: .parse::<u16>() or .parse::<u32>().and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).map_err(...)) for explicit range checking

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> for every line without try_reserve or capacity hint
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation per line; allocation failure propagates as OOM panic rather than typed error; unnecessary heap allocation for a known-two-field grammar
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to parse exactly two fields without Vec allocation, or pre-allocate with try_reserve and use iterators without intermediate collection

findings.problem: println! is a fallible I/O operation that can fail
findings.failure_mode: println! returns io::Result which is ignored; a console I/O failure silently discards the error, potentially hiding terminal/disk issues
findings.fix: Remove the println entirely, or use a proper logging abstraction that returns Result at the shell layer

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation hot path in sensor parsing
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no capacity tracking on Vec)
no command evidence of cargo check/clippy/test/fmt
no second-ring evidence for bounds-check removal or vectorization claims
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse results, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, hidden println side effect, no typed error types, no bounded allocation. Every failure mode in this module panics the process. The function must be refactored to return Result<Vec<Record>, E> with a domain error enum, replace unwrap with propagation, replace as cast with try_from, remove println, and use split_once or get instead of indexing.
